executive_summary: The group reached a tentative decision to lead APAC expansion with Singapore and defer Japan to Q2 next year. Decision quality scores 62/100 — strong on clarity and evidence surfacing, but weak on alternatives analysis, risk mitigation planning, and checkpoint mechanisms. The biggest gap is the absence of explicit go/no-go criteria for the Japan follow-on: the team deferred the decision without defining what would trigger it.
decision_surface: Launch Singapore as lead APAC market in Q4, with Japan as a phased follow-on targeting Q2 next year
strengths: Multiple functional perspectives represented (strategy, sales, finance, engineering) ensuring cross-functional input
Sophie Laurent raised concrete compliance risks (Qualified Invoice System) that shifted the group's framing from aggressive to prudent
The group adapted in real-time — the Singapore-first pivot emerged organically from evidence rather than being imposed top-down
Ravi assigned clear next steps with owners and rough timelines before closing

gaps.gap: No explicit go/no-go criteria for the Japan follow-on decision
gaps.why_it_matters: Without defined criteria, the Japan decision will be re-litigated from scratch at the next meeting, wasting cycles. The group risks either perpetual deferral or premature commitment based on incomplete information.

evidence.speaker: Ravi Patel
evidence.quote: Let's not commit to a Japan timeline today.

evidence.speaker: Sophie Laurent
evidence.quote: We need to be honest with leadership that Japan isn't a Q4 play. It's more like Q2 next year if we're doing it right.

gaps.fix: Define 3-4 specific conditions that must be true before committing to a Japan launch date (e.g., ISMAP certification timeline confirmed, legal review complete, Singapore unit economics validated). Document these as the explicit gate for the Japan decision.

gaps.gap: Legal review not started despite being a critical dependency
gaps.why_it_matters: The Japanese Qualified Invoice System compliance was identified as a deal-breaker for enterprise buyers, yet no legal review has been initiated. This is a known unknown that could invalidate the Japan timeline entirely.

evidence.speaker: Kenji Tanaka
evidence.quote: Not yet. We've been focused on the commercial side. Legal review is on the roadmap but hasn't started.

evidence.speaker: Sophie Laurent
evidence.quote: Manual currency conversion is a compliance nightmare. Japan has strict invoicing requirements under the Qualified Invoice System.

gaps.fix: Assign a named owner to commission the legal review this week with a deadline for preliminary findings. Do not wait for the two-week reconvene — this is on the critical path.

gaps.gap: No discussion of competitive timing or market window
gaps.why_it_matters: The decision to delay Japan was made purely on internal readiness grounds. If competitors are entering the market, the cost of delay may exceed the cost of a rough launch.

evidence.speaker: Ravi Patel
evidence.quote: We've been circling this for two quarters and leadership wants a decision by end of month.

gaps.fix: Before the next meeting, have Kenji provide a brief competitive landscape update for both Singapore and Japan markets, including any known competitor moves in the last 6 months.

assumptions.assumption: Singapore can be served from existing US-East/EU-West infrastructure with acceptable latency
assumptions.how_to_test_fast: Run latency benchmarks from Singapore to US-East and EU-West regions; confirm P95 latency meets SLA requirements for the product's real-time features.

assumptions.assumption: The payments team can deliver a lightweight multi-currency layer in three months
assumptions.how_to_test_fast: Get a written commitment from the payments team lead with a scoped requirements doc and resource allocation confirmation.

assumptions.assumption: Singapore standalone unit economics are viable without the Japan revenue mix
assumptions.how_to_test_fast: Have Kenji model Singapore-only P&L with conservative customer acquisition assumptions and share with Sophie for CFO validation.

assumptions.assumption: The Nomura partnership can be kept warm indefinitely without a firm Japan timeline
assumptions.how_to_test_fast: Have Kenji schedule a call with Nomura's point of contact to gauge their timeline expectations and whether they're evaluating competing partners.

assumptions.assumption: Two weeks is enough time to produce a revised plan, infra estimates, and legal review status
assumptions.how_to_test_fast: Check each owner's calendar and competing priorities for the next two weeks; confirm the legal team can even start a review in that window.

alternatives_missing: Partner-led launch in Japan (e.g., white-label through Nomura) to bypass infrastructure and certification requirements
Acquire a small Japan-based SaaS company with existing ISMAP certification and local infrastructure
Launch a limited pilot in Japan with 2-3 pre-committed enterprise customers under a custom billing arrangement, avoiding the need for full multi-currency billing
Prioritize a different APAC market (e.g., Australia) with lower regulatory complexity than Japan
risks_underweighted: Board perception risk: Singapore-only launch may be seen as insufficient APAC commitment for Series C narrative
Talent risk: no APAC-based engineering or support staff were discussed — customer success in a new timezone is non-trivial
Currency risk: even Singapore has FX exposure (SGD/USD) that wasn't discussed in the unit economics
Opportunity cost: engineering resources allocated to APAC infrastructure compete with core product roadmap

accountability_snapshot.commitment: Deliver revised GTM plan with Singapore as lead market and standalone unit economics
accountability_snapshot.proof_artifact: Revised plan document shared with the team

accountability_snapshot.commitment: Provide firm infrastructure estimate for APAC region buildout
Provide ISMAP certification timeline from compliance team
Reconvene the group in two weeks with revised plan, infra estimates, and legal review status
accountability_snapshot.proof_artifact: Meeting scheduled with agenda covering all three items

decision_hygiene_upgrades_next_meeting: Open with a recap of the decision criteria — what must be true for us to proceed with Singapore? With Japan?
Assign a pre-read: circulate Kenji's revised plan and Diana's infra estimates 48 hours before the meeting so discussion time is spent on debate, not presentation
Explicitly ask 'What alternatives have we not considered?' before closing the decision
End with a written decision statement that all attendees confirm: 'We are deciding X, contingent on Y, with Z as the checkpoint date'
Time-box the Japan discussion separately from Singapore to avoid conflation

single_most_important_upgrade.upgrade: Define explicit go/no-go criteria for the Japan follow-on decision before the next meeting
single_most_important_upgrade.why: Without criteria, the Japan question will consume disproportionate meeting time and remain unresolved. Clear gates (e.g., ISMAP timeline confirmed, legal review complete, Singapore month-1 metrics) convert an ambiguous deferral into a structured decision framework.
single_most_important_upgrade.success_signal: A written list of 3-5 conditions is shared with the team before the next meeting, and the meeting opens by reviewing progress against those conditions.
